title: KL Rahul Retires Hurt as Padikkal's Unbeaten 131 Powers India on Day 1 in Galle
excerpt: India closed the opening day of the first Test against Sri Lanka at 288 for 2, with Devdutt Padikkal scoring a brilliant century and KL Rahul departing with cramps after a composed 77.
body:
• India dominated Day 1 of the first Test in Galle, finishing at 288/2 after winning the toss and electing to bat on August 15.
  • KL Rahul retired hurt with cramps after scoring 77 off 162 balls, raising concerns about his availability for the remainder of the match.
  • Devdutt Padikkal struck an unbeaten 131 off 178 balls, his highest Test score, anchoring India's innings alongside Rishabh Pant (27* off 36).
  • India are playing without Jasprit Bumrah (knee), Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy, and Washington Sundar — all sidelined with injuries.

India seized control of the opening day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle on Friday, reaching 288 for 2 at stumps, powered by a commanding unbeaten century from Devdutt Padikkal. However, the day was marred by a worrying moment when vice-captain KL Rahul retired hurt with cramps after building a patient innings of 77.

Rahul's Injury Scare

Rahul, batting at number two, had looked in excellent touch during his 162-ball innings that included nine fours and a six. The 34-year-old had helped stabilize India after the early loss of Yashasvi Jaiswal and was building a crucial partnership when cramps forced him to leave the field.

India's coaching staff confirmed that Rahul's retirement was a precautionary measure, describing the cramps as a product of the humid conditions in Galle rather than a structural injury. However, the development will be closely monitored given Rahul's injury history and his importance to the batting lineup as vice-captain under Shubman Gill.

Padikkal's Career-Best Knock

While Rahul's departure raised questions, Padikkal provided all the answers India needed. The left-hander walked in after Jaiswal's run-out — the opener was dismissed for 32 off 37 balls after a miscommunication — and proceeded to bat with remarkable composure and authority.

Padikkal's unbeaten 131 off 178 deliveries, studded with 12 fours and a six, was a statement innings from a player who has been on the fringes of India's Test squad. Against a Sri Lankan attack that struggled to find consistent lines on a surface offering little lateral movement, Padikkal was particularly strong through the covers and showed excellent footwork against spin.

Captain Shubman Gill's stay at the crease was brief — he was caught by Lahiru Udara off the bowling of a Sri Lankan bowler — but Rishabh Pant ensured the momentum did not stall. The wicketkeeper-batsman was unbeaten on 27 off 36 balls at stumps, having struck three fours and a six in typically aggressive fashion.

Sri Lanka's Bowling Woes

Sri Lanka's bowling attack, led by Dhananjaya de Silva's captaincy, had a forgettable outing. Left-arm spinner Keshara Nuwantha bowled 21 overs without taking a wicket, conceding 98 runs. The absence of a potent fast-bowling option was evident throughout the day as India's batsmen scored at close to four runs per over.

The hosts' task is compounded by the fact that Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, and Asitha Fernando could not generate the breakthroughs needed on a pitch that is expected to offer more turn as the match progresses.

Series Context

The two-match series carries significant weight in the World Test Championship standings, with India and Sri Lanka currently occupying fifth and sixth place, respectively. India are already without pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who is sidelined with a knee injury, along with Harshit Rana (hamstring), Nitish Kumar Reddy (quad), and Washington Sundar (hamstring).

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, the series represents a chance to see a transitioning Indian side — now led by Gill with Rahul as vice-captain — prove itself away from home. The second Test is scheduled for August 23-27 in Colombo.
